clue.text: A hoard of coins reported

indicators.note: reported means the word for coins is to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: money in coins is cash

explanation.surface: Someone tells of a hidden hoard of coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' tells you CASH is said aloud, giving the sound of CACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store or stockpile of valuables.

clue.text: Islanders initially called yesterday, perturbed by civil disturbances

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: riots are outbreaks of civil disorder

explanation.surface: Islanders were phoned yesterday, upset by unrest at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers called, yesterday and perturbed, giving C, Y, P; 'perturbed' looks like an emotion but only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cypriots are natives of Cyprus, an island in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: The crewman with the money-bag, right?…

parts.note: a purse is a small bag for money

explanation.surface: A query whether a certain sailor holds the ship's money.
explanation.definitionFit: A purser is the ship's officer in charge of accounts and passengers' welfare.

clue.text: …and another crewman, consumed by money

indicators.note: by means the eating word sits right next to the money letter, placed after it

parts.note: consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Following on, a second sailor is eaten up by greed for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues the previous one with its leading dots; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a deck officer on a merchant ship, ranking below the captain.

clue.text: Copy is just the average rubbish

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A complaint that imitation is merely mediocre junk.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or imitate mindlessly, as the bird mimics speech.

clue.text: Kindly disposed — that is to say, intended to be

explanation.surface: A clarification that someone's goodwill was meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is to say' links the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-meant describes good-natured intentions; read as two words it says something was meant to be well, that is, intended to turn out fine.

clue.text: An idle girl, yet of some use on board

parts.note: idle means lazy
Susan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lazy young woman who nonetheless proves useful on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship but means a dining table, where the revolving tray sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating serving tray placed in the middle of a dining table is handy for passing dishes.

clue.text: A refuge that could be paradise if in the east

indicators.note: if in says the word for paradise would be complete were the east letter put in, so it is removed here

parts.note: heaven is paradise
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A shelter that would be heavenly if located in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a safe harbour or place of shelter.

clue.text: Unemotional when a good man is foul-smelling

parts.note: ST, for saint, is crossword shorthand for a good man
olid is a rare word meaning rank or stinking

explanation.surface: A stoic is said to be impassive when a virtuous person stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: OLID is an uncommon word for foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive, showing little feeling.

clue.text: Splinters difficult to see aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard puts the word for difficult inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
hard means difficult

explanation.surface: Tiny fragments that are hard to spot on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Shards are sharp broken fragments, as splinters are.

clue.text: When inisled, housekeepers' fury is contained completely

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'When inisled, housekeepers' fury is contained completely'. The parse is NT (housekeepers) + IRE (fury) inside ELY, the Isle of Ely; 'inisled' must both name the isle ELY and signal the insertion, a word doing two jobs, or the text is garbled (perhaps 'in Ely').
annotationWithheld.clue: When inisled, housekeepers' fury is contained completely

clue.text: A hot rock — free!

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or outcrop
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A blazing stone is liberated.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid means scorching or very hot.

clue.text: Game to bring violin back

indicators.note: back means the word for the violin is read backwards

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: A game played to return a fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns STRAD round; 'to bring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game of throwing small missiles at a board.

clue.text: For example, a landlord

explanation.surface: An illustration of what a property owner is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is itself an example of an alphabet character; a landlord is one who lets property.
explanation.definitionFit: A is one alphabet character, so it is an instance of a written symbol; someone who lets property out is a lessor.

clue.text: Fie, 'tis sad to find another replete!

indicators.note: another means these letters form a different word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A lament that someone else has eaten their fill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find another' asks for a rearrangement of FIE TIS SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means full after eating, or contented.

clue.text: The bulk of the service

explanation.surface: Most of a church ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass is the main body or bulk of something; it is also the Eucharist service in church.

clue.text: Ban on journalist exposed

parts.note: to bar is to ban
ED, editor, is crossword shorthand for a journalist

explanation.surface: A ban on a reporter is made public.
explanation.definitionFit: Bared means uncovered or laid open.

clue.text: Deck should be neat

parts.note: trim means neat and tidy

explanation.surface: A ship's deck ought to be tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like part of a ship but is the verb, to adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To betrim is to decorate or adorn, as deck does.

clue.text: The air, for some reason, gaseous

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Air is gaseous, for some reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The air' suggests the atmosphere, matching gaseous, but means a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody or tune.

clue.text: Accommodation I take on for nag

parts.note: a stall is accommodation for a horse in a stable

explanation.surface: Someone takes on lodgings for an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is a horse, and an uncastrated male horse is one kind.

clue.text: Change direction for Roman fountain — back to fifth roundabout

indicators.note: fifth picks the fifth letter of roundabout
back means the name of the fountain is read in reverse

parts.note: the Trevi Fountain is the famous fountain in Rome

explanation.surface: Instructions to reroute traffic for a fountain in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' suggests a traffic circle but merely lends its fifth letter D; 'to' joins it to IVERT, TREVI turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert is to turn aside or reroute.

clue.text: What the journalist did — tee off?

definitions.text: What the journalist did — tee off?

indicators.note: off means the letters of the two words are in disorder

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a reporter's job is to start a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals a rearrangement of DID and TEE; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor's work is revising and correcting copy.

clue.text: Run out of clothes

explanation.surface: Running out wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak is a run of luck or wins; to streak is to dash naked in public.

clue.text: Jack, for example — an awful tearaway!

explanation.surface: Jack is a terrible tearaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tearaway' reads as a hooligan but splits as one who tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack was the notorious Victorian London murderer; one who tears things apart rips them.

clue.text: Take off football gear

explanation.surface: Removing one's football kit.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to undress; a team's strip is its kit of shirts and shorts.

clue.text: A functionary not on one CIA list to begin with

parts.note: off means not on
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to begin with takes the first letter of list

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat missing from a CIA roster.
explanation.definitionFit: An official is a person holding an office, a functionary.

clue.text: Spare list

explanation.surface: A two-word note of a thin list.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean means thin or spare; to list is to tilt or lean over.

clue.text: A friend gets a note on taste

parts.note: a pal is a friend
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A friend gives an opinion on someone's taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The palate is a person's sense of flavour or discernment.

clue.text: Purchase a feast on returning

indicators.note: on returning means the word for a feast is read backwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively feast or celebration

explanation.surface: Buying a banquet on coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' suggests buying, but means grip or leverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase is leverage, mechanical advantage gained by a bar or pulley.

clue.text: A clan ode I got wrong in old Scotland

indicators.note: got wrong means these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Highland poem botched by its writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, now poetic.
